countries.name: Denmark
countries.jurisdiction_note: Denmark decides residence through two agencies sharing the nyidanmark.dk portal: SIRI (the Danish Agency for International Recruitment and Integration) decides work and study routes, and the Danish Immigration Service (Udlændingestyrelsen) decides visitor, family and permanent-residence routes. visa_sources.authority carries the deciding agency for each route. Greenland and the Faroe Islands run separate immigration rules and are not covered by these routes.

countries.name: Egypt
countries.immigration_authority: Ministry of Interior — Arab Republic of Egypt

countries.name: Finland
countries.foreign_affairs_authority: Ulkoministeriö (Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland)
countries.jurisdiction_note: Finland splits entry between two authorities. Residence permits are Migri's, and migri.fi is readable by an identified agent. Short-stay Schengen visas are the Ministry for Foreign Affairs', and um.fi returns 403 to the same agent, so no Finnish short-stay visa type is registered. Migri publishes an authoritative English tree at /en/ -- unlike Migrationsverket, whose English pages are summaries -- so sources are English and directly reviewable.

countries.name: France
countries.foreign_affairs_authority: Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères (France-Visas)
countries.jurisdiction_note: Sources are published by Service-Public.gouv.fr (DILA, a service of the Prime Minister), the French State's official public-service publisher. DILA describes the rules; it does not decide applications. A visa is issued by France-Visas (Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères) and a residence permit is decided by the préfecture of the applicant's department. france-visas.gouv.fr returns HTTP 403 on robots.txt to our monitor from two separate egress paths, so it is not registered and is not read. Overseas territories (outre-mer) have entry rules of their own and are not covered by these routes.

countries.name: Hong Kong SAR
countries.immigration_authority: Immigration Department of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
countries.jurisdiction_note: Hong Kong is part of the People's Republic of China and administers its own immigration under the Basic Law, so it is registered as its own destination rather than under CN. A PRC passport does not admit its holder: mainland Chinese residents are expressly excluded from the General Employment Policy and routed to the Admission Scheme for Mainland Talents and Professionals. Macao SAR residents, Taiwan residents and overseas Chinese holding PRC passports each have their own arrangements on the same pages. No separate foreign affairs authority is recorded -- the Immigration Department issues visas and entry permits itself, and the Office of the Commissioner of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs handles a different set of questions. Since 28 December 2021 visas are issued as "e-Visa" only.

countries.name: Japan
countries.immigration_authority: Immigration Services Agency (出入国在留管理庁)
countries.jurisdiction_note: Japan splits the decision in two. The Immigration Services Agency, an external bureau of the Ministry of Justice, defines and grants the residence STATUS — that is what these sources publish. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs issues the VISA through embassies and consulates, and www.mofa.go.jp returns HTTP 403 on robots.txt to our monitor, so it is not registered and is not read. A reader who needs the visa application procedure will not find it here. All sources are in Japanese; English labels in the requirements are VisaAI translations, not the authority's wording.

countries.name: Jordan
countries.jurisdiction_note: Coverage is ONE route. Jordan's national eGovernment portal publishes a visa guide naming the ways into the Kingdom and the e-visa document list. The Ministry of Interior's own site reads at 9,862 characters with no requirement language, its entry-procedure page returns HTTP 500, and its e-services host does not complete a connection from production. Fees are deferred by the portal to the official visa site and are not published here. Sources are Arabic; English labels in the requirements are VisaAI translations.

countries.name: Malaysia
countries.immigration_authority: Jabatan Imigresen Malaysia (Immigration Department of Malaysia)
countries.foreign_affairs_authority: Kementerian Luar Negeri Malaysia (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
countries.jurisdiction_note: Malaysia routes several passes through a sector body BEFORE the Immigration Department sees them: EMGS (Education Malaysia Global Services) screens students and the Ministry of Home Affairs authorises the institution; the Expatriate Committee and sector regulators approve expatriates. The Immigration Department endorses and issues. Sabah and Sarawak administer their own immigration under the Malaysia Agreement and add state-specific documents, which the Department states on the same pages. Only pages whose content is distinct from the site navigation are registered as sources -- imi.gov.my serves an identical 820-line menu on every page, and several of its pages are nothing else.

countries.name: Oman
countries.jurisdiction_note: THIS DESTINATION COVERS WORK PERMITS, NOT ENTRY VISAS. The Ministry of Labour authorises the EMPLOYMENT of non-Omani workers and publishes these sources. Entry and residence are decided by the Royal Oman Police, whose e-Visa portal serves its visa catalogue as client-rendered script — 44,892 bytes normalising to 927 characters — so no entry-visa requirement can be read. Nobody has refused us; there is no text. A worker needs BOTH a Ministry of Labour work permit and an ROP visa, and only the first is published here. Sources are Arabic; English labels in the requirements are VisaAI translations.

countries.name: Portugal
countries.immigration_authority: AIMA — Agência para a Integração, Migrações e Asilo
countries.foreign_affairs_authority: Ministério dos Negócios Estrangeiros (Portal dos Vistos)
countries.jurisdiction_note: AIMA decides RESIDENCE PERMITS and publishes these sources. It does not issue visas. The MFA visa portal (vistos.mne.gov.pt) drops our production source address at the TCP level — the connection is reset after ClientHello and behaves identically for every request shape we can offer, so it is a decision about our address rather than about our request. It answers 200 from a second egress. It is not registered and is not read. Several routes below therefore require a residence visa whose own conditions we cannot publish. Sources are Portuguese; AIMA publishes an English FAQ for the investment route only. The Azores and Madeira are covered by these routes; Portuguese consular posts abroad are not an AIMA competence.

countries.name: Qatar
countries.foreign_affairs_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Consular Affairs Department
countries.jurisdiction_note: Coverage is ONE route: the fee schedule for visas issued by Qatari missions abroad through the automated system. The Ministry of Interior decides entry and holds the eligibility detail; portal.moi.gov.qa serves 70KB of markup carrying under 2,000 characters with 85% shared between sibling pages, its e-services host does not complete a connection from production, and hukoomi.gov.qa returns HTTP 403 despite robots.txt permitting the path. So this destination publishes what a visa COSTS and not who qualifies for it.

countries.name: Singapore
countries.jurisdiction_note: Singapore splits entry between two authorities and both are readable by an identified agent. The Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA) decides who may ENTER -- entry visas, visit passes, Student's Pass, Long-Term Visit Pass. The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) decides who may WORK -- Employment Pass, S Pass, EntrePass, ONE Pass, Work Permit, Dependant's Pass -- and for every MOM pass the APPLICANT IS THE EMPLOYER, not the worker. Sources are therefore registered against whichever of the two authorities actually owns the rule, and authority_rank is 1 for both: neither is secondary to the other, they simply govern different questions.

countries.name: Sweden
countries.jurisdiction_note: Requirements are sourced from Migrationsverket's SWEDISH pages. The English site is a summary that states no requirements, and Migrationsverket's sitemap contains no /English/ URLs at all. Fees are quoted in EUR because the Schengen visa fee is set in EUR, while the maintenance requirement is in SEK.

countries.name: Thailand
countries.immigration_authority: Immigration Bureau, Royal Thai Police (สำนักงานตรวจคนเข้าเมือง)
countries.foreign_affairs_authority: Department of Consular Affairs, Ministry of Foreign Affairs (กรมการกงสุล)
countries.jurisdiction_note: Thailand splits the decision. The Department of Consular Affairs (MFA) issues the VISA abroad and publishes these sources. The Immigration Bureau of the Royal Thai Police decides admission, length of stay in the Kingdom, extensions and changes of visa type — and www.immigration.go.th returns HTTP 403 to our monitor despite robots.txt permitting the path, so it is not registered. Every route here therefore states how to OBTAIN a visa and defers the stay itself to an authority we cannot read. All sources are Thai; English labels in the requirements are VisaAI translations. The department's own English pages are dated 2017 and are deliberately not used.
